title: HighLevel Will Now Score Your LinkedIn Ads. It Still Cannot Build Them.
desc: HighLevel extended Opportunity Score to Google and LinkedIn on August 10. Ask AI excluded LinkedIn by name on August 4, so scoring is wider than automation.
keywords: highlevel opportunity score, gohighlevel ad manager linkedin, gohighlevel google ads keywords, highlevel ad manager update, gohighlevel for agencies
cta: Want your client ad accounts and CRM run as one system?
body:
August 11, 2026. HighLevel extended its Ad Manager Opportunity Score to Google and LinkedIn campaigns on August 10, six days after putting an AI campaign builder into the same product. The two releases do not cover the same platforms, and the gap between them is the useful part.

What shipped on August 10

  1. Opportunity Score now covers Meta, Google and LinkedIn in the Ad Manager campaign builders, per HighLevel's changelog. It was Meta only at launch.
  2. It is a 0 to 100 readiness score on the pre publish Review screen, summarised as Low, Medium or High, with suggestions grouped into areas such as Audience, Budget, Creative, Tracking and Keywords.
  3. HighLevel says twice that it is advisory. The changelog states the score is guidance rather than a guarantee of campaign performance, and that recommendations do not automatically modify campaign settings.
  4. The same day, the 40 keyword limit was removed for both positive and negative keywords on Google campaigns, with bulk paste separated by new lines or commas and automatic cleanup of duplicates and blanks.

Scoring is now wider than automation

On August 4 HighLevel put its Ask AI assistant inside Ad Manager so agencies could build and manage campaigns by describing them. That release excluded four surfaces by name, and the first one listed was LinkedIn Ads. Six days later, LinkedIn gets a readiness score.

So inside one product you can now be told that your LinkedIn audience targeting, budget, creatives, destination URLs and lead generation setup are weak, and you cannot ask the assistant to fix any of it. The diagnostic surface is running ahead of the automation surface. That is the normal order for a vendor shipping AI next to live ad spend, and it is worth knowing before you tell a client the platform handles LinkedIn.

The keyword change matters more than it looks, for the same reason. Opportunity Score for Google reviews keywords among its areas, and until August 10 you could not act on a keyword recommendation past 40 entries. That cap bit hardest on negative keywords, because a waste control list is normally far longer than the positive list it protects.

What it means for operators

The first thing to paste into the enlarged field is the negative list, not more positive keywords. Most underperforming Google Search accounts are not short of match types. They are paying for traffic that a 200 line negative list would have removed, and until this week the builder would not accept the list.

Treat the score itself as a checklist that catches omissions, not as a forecast. It reads configuration, so it can tell you a conversion action is missing and it cannot tell you the offer is wrong. If you run client ad accounts alongside a CRM, that split is exactly where GoHighLevel work earns its money, and where an AI automation agency should be straight with clients that a readiness score is the cheap half of the job.
faqs: It is a 0 to 100 campaign readiness score shown on the pre publish Review screen in HighLevel Ad Manager, summarised as Low, Medium or High. It reviews campaign configuration and returns prioritised suggestions grouped into areas such as Audience, Budget, Creative, Tracking and Keywords. As of August 10, 2026 it covers Meta, Google and LinkedIn campaigns.
Does Opportunity Score change my campaign automatically?

No. HighLevel's changelog states that recommendations do not automatically modify campaign settings and that the score is guidance rather than a guarantee of campaign performance. Selecting a suggestion navigates you to the relevant campaign section so you can make the change yourself.
Can HighLevel's Ask AI build LinkedIn campaigns?

No. When Ask AI shipped inside Ad Manager on August 4, 2026, HighLevel named four excluded surfaces, and LinkedIn Ads was one of them, alongside Workflows, Templates and Snapshots. Ask AI covers Meta and Google campaign types. LinkedIn now receives an Opportunity Score but cannot be built by the assistant.
How many keywords can a HighLevel Google campaign have now?

There is no longer a 40 keyword cap. On August 10, 2026 HighLevel removed the limit for both positive and negative keywords in Google Ads campaigns and added bulk paste, accepting keywords separated by new lines or commas, with duplicates and blank entries removed automatically. Keyword eligibility still follows Google Ads requirements.
